story.head: Active D vs. Forward-led
paras: The Flyers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Buffalo on Oct 21. The Flyers (5-10-6) lost 3-2 in overtime to Edmonton on Wednesday, and the Sabres are winless in three (0-2-1). Going in, the Sabres are sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 18th in the NHL) and the Flyers seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 27th).
This season, the Sabres have been outscored 67-55, but only 40-38 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 21-11.

The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (5th), but don't block many shots (30th). They also get their defensemen shooting (5th), so their defensemen shoot a lot, and the Flyers’ not so much. As for the Flyers, they play slow, tight games (2nd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (31st). They also block a lot of shots (4th), and the Sabres’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. Philadelphia has scored 2.24 goals a game, the second fewest in the league.

Tage Thompson (12 G / 9 A / 21 P in 19 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring. Jack Quinn (9 G / 10 A / 19 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind, with a point in six straight games against Philadelphia. For the Flyers, Matvei Michkov (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring. Trevor Zegras (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 21 GP) is next in line, with a point in five straight games against Buffalo.

Buffalo has two options in net: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (5-4-3 / .867 SV% in 11 GS) and Colten Ellis (3-3-0 / .873 SV% in 7 GS). Luukkonen has started five of their last ten games, including the last one on Wednesday. Philadelphia also has two options: Dan Vladař (3-4-4 / .879 SV% in 11 GS) and Joseph Woll (2-6-2 / .901 SV% in 10 GS). Vladař has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Wednesday. For both teams, it’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
